internal_decisions: The SKU and qty checks are private module helpers.
Sort key is (quantity, sku) over inv.items()

plan: Baseline: tests (11) and acceptance (10) all pass.
Contracts: WP-02 consumption of Inventory.items() checked, including no mutation and the copy.
Edge cases: non-string SKUs, huge ints, failed calls leaving state unchanged, thresholds of 0 or negative, empty inventory and unicode SKUs. Added in qa/test_qa.py and all green.
Integration: covered by the contract and edge tests, since the only flow is stock into report.
Discarded: regression (no prior code beyond the version), non-functional (not in architecture), concurrency (excluded). Re-run: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa
gaps: Python 3.9 compatibility was not tested because only the local interpreter is available.
Concurrency is out of scope, so it was not tested.

advisory.problem: Test names don't contain the AC-NNN ID. They do match the Check names in the brief, so the mapping is traceable.
advisory.evidence: Names such as test_sku_is_normalised have no AC-001. This doesn't let a wrong implementation pass.

advisory.problem: AC-003 never tests a bad qty on remove when the SKU is unknown or has too little stock. A different validation order (the stock check before the qty check) would go unnoticed. The brief doesn't require it.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that raises InsufficientStock for remove('Q', 0) is not tested.
